scopeNote: This is a bounded sweep of high-value public research leads for inland, marine and estuarine coverage. It is not a complete review of all 36 waterbody leads, a fish distribution baseline, or an absence assessment.

sourceAbstractFacts.durationDescription: two-year study; exact sampling dates not verified from the official article page

followUpSources.accessReview: Official publisher article page and indexed primary article text reviewed, including its seven-lake scope and Table 1 lake names. Direct PDF retrieval returned an interactive JavaScript/cookie challenge; no local copy or bypass.
followUpSources.reuseReview: No item-specific reuse license verified. Current publisher submission guidance says authors must submit a signed Mandatory Copyright Transfer; the signed form for this 2017 article was not inspected. Per-lake species rows remain quarantined.
limits: The abstract's ten fish species and 5,166 individuals are aggregate historical study facts, not per-lake species assignments or a current census.
Table 1 supports lake identity and location context, but no coordinates or lake geometry are adopted in the scope registry.
No per-lake species rows are copied or admitted until item-specific rights are confirmed.
The article's historic survey does not establish present-day abundance, legality, safety or fishing permission.

limits: Exact locality strings do not cover spelling variants, records lacking locality text, or coordinate-only records.

sources.bibliography: Paller, V. G. V., Corpuz, M. N. C., & Ocampo, P. P. (2013). Diversity and distribution of freshwater fish assemblages in Tayabas River, Quezon (Philippines). Philippine Journal of Science, 142(1), 55-67.
sources.accessReview: Official PJS/SEAFDEC metadata and abstract were readable through indexed source results. Direct publisher page/PDF requests returned 403 during review; SEAFDEC item metadata lists no associated file. No original PDF or Table 1 was acquired for this batch.
sources.reuseReview: No item-specific reuse license was verified. The PJS author guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form, but that current policy does not establish the exact rights for this 2013 article. Open-access visibility is not treated as table-reuse permission.
limits: The abstract's three stream sections are not precise site coordinates or river-wide geometry.
2010 sampling is historical and not a current-presence report.
No salinity values or source-matched brackish designation were reviewed.

sources.bibliography: Torres, F. S. B. Jr., Bendaño, A. P., Lopez, G. D. V., Perez, M. A., & Santos, M. D. (2017). Species composition, distribution, biomass trends and exploitation of dominant fish species in Manila Bay using experimental trawl survey.

sourceTableFacts.tableTitleScope: Top 50 fish and invertebrate species by biomass abundance, summarized by province
sourceTableFacts.commonnessMarksDescribe: frequency-of-hauls bands, not individual fish counts
sourceTableFacts.interpretation: The 100 Cavite-group total is mixed fish and invertebrate species, not 100 fish species; it is a historical survey summary, not a current checklist.

sources.accessReview: Official NFRDI item metadata and the complete 16-page primary PDF were reviewed; the abstract and Table 3.2 confirm the 16-station study and a province-grouped Cavite summary. The station map has not been georeferenced.
sources.reuseReview: No item-specific reuse license was found on the 2017 item/PDF. The journal's current CC BY-NC 4.0 policy is not assumed to apply retroactively to this 2017 article; table rows remain held pending written/item-specific rights confirmation.
limits: The paper groups one historical trawling sector under Cavite, but does not provide a georeferenced municipal-water boundary or prove all 16 stations fall within Cavite.
The 100 Cavite-group species total includes fish and invertebrates; the table separately reports 24 fish species in its summary, and neither count is a current checklist.
The 146 paper-wide total includes fish and invertebrates and must not be presented as a fish-only species total.
No individual table species rows are admitted or reproduced while article-specific reuse rights remain unverified.
Study-period trawl evidence does not establish present abundance, fishing permission or safety.

sources.accessReview: Official NFRDI repository metadata reviewed. The 51.49-MB poster image was not downloaded or visually inspected.
sources.reuseReview: No poster-image or derived-data reuse terms verified. Do not copy the image or assume its species and size table is reusable.
limits: The repository abstract lists nine taxa although the item title says Top 10; the missing tenth is unknown.
The item concerns Balayan/Calatagan Bay, not all Batangas waters or CALABARZON.
Maximum size and common/local names require direct poster review and identity checks before any use.

sources.accessReview: Official NFRDI FY2023 annual-report search-index text was reviewed, including its Pansipit summary. Opening the repository's bitstream view returned a login page; no full report or underlying species table was acquired.
sources.reuseReview: No explicit reuse license for the report or underlying catch data was verified. The summary is a source lead only; no species rows are extracted.
limits: Landing-center catch composition is not a complete river inventory or abundance estimate for the whole river.
The 38 total includes non-finfish groups; it is not 38 fish species.
No station-specific salinity or brackish classification is provided in the reviewed summary.

sources.accessReview: Official NFRDI announcement and repository metadata describe the NFRDI-LLDA assessment partnership; no assessment results were supplied in the announcement.
sources.reuseReview: No fish data are present to reuse or admit. Re-check the official repository when the assessment outputs are released.
limits: A planned assessment is not a species occurrence source.
Do not substitute older lake checklists or fisheries summaries for the new assessment's unpublished results.
The four selected records have null GBIF class fields and were reviewed against the Field Museum fish-collection dataset, specimen basis, taxon, family and catalog number.
All four records share one coordinate with no uncertainty value and retain GBIF quality flags; the projection omits the coordinate.
This open-data batch is separate from the 2023 NFRDI landing-center report, which remains held pending source access and reuse review.
Historical locality records do not establish current presence, an exact river reach, salinity or a complete fish inventory.

regionalGapSummary.freshwater: The four 1933 Pansipit River GBIF specimens support historical locality evidence only. Tayabas River remains a strong historical study lead, but the original species table and article-specific reuse terms remain unverified. Laguna de Bay's NFRDI-LLDA assessment is a future source opportunity, not current data.
regionalGapSummary.marine: The full NFRDI Manila Bay trawl paper is acquired and reviewed, including a historic Cavite-group table summary; item-specific reuse rights and station georeferencing remain open, so zero species assertions are admitted. Balayan/Calatagan remains a metadata/poster lead.
regionalGapSummary.brackishEstuarine: The five existing held leads still yield zero admitted assertions. No new source in this sweep verifies fish identities joined to measured station salinity under reusable terms.
regionalGapSummary.smallLakesWetlandsReservoirs: A historical survey source now covers all seven named San Pablo crater lakes, but item-specific reuse rights block per-lake species rows. Other small lakes, wetlands and reservoirs remain source and coverage gaps.

nextActions: Continue with sources whose full table and item-specific reuse terms can be checked without login or access-control bypass; do not wait for NAMRIA or other email replies.

Prioritize the original Tayabas River article/table and NFRDI Pansipit report for access and rights review; keep the latter separate from the CC0 museum specimens and preserve its landing-center scope.
Seek item-specific permission for the 2017 Manila Bay table and a source-ready station dataset/map; do not turn the Cavite-group summary into current presence or a municipal-water boundary.
Check the Balayan/Calatagan poster's tenth taxon and item-specific terms only if direct access becomes available; do not republish its image.
Seek item-specific rights clarification or an eligible alternative dataset for the seven San Pablo lakes; continue named small-lake, wetland and reservoir sources beyond that study.
Publish an L1 coverage-and-gap report before advancing to NCR; zero admissions here does not mean the waterbodies lack fish.
nonClaims: No species assertions from these five leads were admitted into the app.
No blanket Creative Commons or public-domain status was inferred for journal tables, NFRDI reports or poster imagery.

No email or data request was sent, and no login, payment or access-control bypass was used.
